name: Ethnographic Contextual Inquiry (Shadowing)
phase: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [operators] face unrecorded cognitive overload while [operating system X]. We will verify this by observing 6 operators in their natural workplace for 4 hours each, and consider it validated if we record ≥ 5 unprompted compensatory mechanisms (e.g., sticky notes, personal spreadsheets, ad-hoc scripts) per operator per shift.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Clear confidentiality and access; build a ledger for micro-interruptions, non-verbal cues and app switches.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Observe silently through a shift; interrupt only on a deviation and ask what motivated that step.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Compile a minute-by-minute trace of application switches, error recovery, movement and distraction.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Execute confidentiality agreements and workplace access protocols. Construct an observation ledger focused on micro-interruptions, non-verbal cues, and application-switching frequency.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Observe the operator silently during regular shifts. Interrupt only when an operational deviation occurs: "I observed you copied that string into an external editor before pasting it. What motivated that step?"

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Compile a minute-by-minute workflow trace logging application switches, error recovery efforts, physical movements, and environmental distractions.

warning.label: Hawthorne Effect
warning.text: Observed operators tidy their workarounds and follow formal protocol because someone is watching.

warningFull: Subjects alter their conventional workflows, adhere more strictly to formal protocols, or tidy operational workarounds simply because they are being observed.
